clue.text: Responsible writer from our point of view

definitions.text: Responsible writer from our point of view

parts.note: surface reading: an author who writes responsibly
setter's reading: the setter signs as Biggles, so the writer responsible for this setter's namesake is the creator of Biggles

explanation.walkthrough: The setter's pseudonym is Biggles, the flying ace of boys' adventure books, and his creator was Captain W. E. Johns; from the setter's point of view he is the responsible writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain W. E. Johns created the Biggles books, so he is the author answerable for the setter's adopted name.

clue.text: Abnormal growth restricting a beast

parts.note: a wart is a small abnormal growth on the skin
to hog something is to keep it to yourself, restricting others' use

explanation.surface: A tumour is pressing on some animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The warthog is a wild African pig, an animal and so a beast; aptly, it carries wart-like lumps on its face.

clue.text: I only want to touch my man, but this causes commotion in gallery!

definitions.text: I only want to touch my man

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: a jube is a rood loft, a gallery dividing nave from chancel in a church
ado is fuss or commotion

explanation.surface: A chess player apologising for touching a piece, yet causing uproar among spectators in the gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: J'adoube (French, 'I adjust') is what a chess player says when touching a piece only to straighten it, so as not to be bound to move it. The gallery suggests spectators; it is a church loft.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase is the formal declaration that a player is merely adjusting, not moving, one of their own pieces.

clue.text: Handle cobbling together with elves?

indicators.note: cobbling together suggests joining pieces, here the letters spanning two neighbouring words

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the join between the two words

explanation.surface: A nod to the fairy tale of the shoemaker whose shoes were cobbled together overnight by elves.
explanation.walkthrough: Cobbling and elves call up the shoemaker story and an anagram, but the letters of elves cannot make the answer; it sits across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A helve is the wooden handle of an axe, hammer or similar tool.

clue.text: A little flower American left in road

indicators.note: these letters are placed inside the following word

parts.note: a street is a road in a town
AM is the standard abbreviation for American
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An American bloom has been left lying in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: Flower is the old crossword trick for a river, something that flows, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamlet is a small stream, and a stream is something that flows, so a little flower in the watery sense.

clue.text: One must be cracked

parts.note: setter's reading: a person who is mentally unhinged, cracked in the slang sense
surface reading: the shell of a nut has to be cracked open to get at the kernel

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the clue is about a nut in its shell; the answer is slang for someone who is crazy, which is also what cracked means.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an eccentric or crazy person; cracked is likewise slang for mentally unbalanced.

clue.text: Might I live off berries? Yes, we have no bananas

parts.note: taken as written
bananas is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A forager wonders about a diet of berries, and the reply quotes the old song 'Yes! We Have No Bananas'.
explanation.walkthrough: The bananas belong to the old song in the surface, but bananas also means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer with no settled home, who might well survive by foraging wild fruit along the way.

clue.text: Formidable woman ate Grant Mitchell's head in a stew

indicators.note: something in a stew is in a muddle, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a name is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the surname

explanation.surface: A fierce woman devoured the head of Grant Mitchell in a casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: Grant Mitchell is a hard-man character in the BBC soap EastEnders, which makes the stew seem like a domestic scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a scolding, overbearing woman, the name coming from an imagined deity in medieval mystery plays.

clue.text: Paul's monkey puzzling lost in its bowels?

indicators.note: puzzling suggests confused, so the letters are jumbled
the bowels are the inside, so this goes within the other word

parts.note: an ape is a monkey in the loose sense
the fodder rearranged

explanation.surface: A monkey puzzle tree seems to have lost something deep inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: Monkey puzzle is a tree, which hides the separate ape and anagram signal. It also nods to Araucaria, Latin for the monkey puzzle and the pseudonym of a famous setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Paul is counted as an apostle, one of the early missionaries sent out to spread Christianity.

clue.text: Another handle needed to rotate peg about the centre

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other
turning something around makes it read the other way

parts.note: a tee is a golfer's peg
pith is the central core of something

explanation.surface: Fixing something requires a second handle to turn a peg round its middle.
explanation.walkthrough: Handle is slang for a name, picking up 3-down where it meant a tool's grip.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is a descriptive name or nickname, and handle is informal for a name or title.

clue.text: Enigmatist sees Python regular carrying dead parrot's insides outside

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it inside
the insides of a word are its middle letters

parts.note: the two letters at the very centre of the word

indicators.note: these letters go round the outside of the rest

parts.note: Eric Idle was a regular member of the Monty Python team
D is the abbreviation for dead

explanation.surface: A puzzler watches a Monty Python star doing the famous dead parrot sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: The dead parrot sketch is Monty Python's most famous routine, so the surface stays inside the show.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigmatist sets enigmas, and someone who poses conundrums is a maker of puzzles in that sense.

clue.text: Telegraph man and his politics accepted by European Union man

indicators.note: what is accepted is taken in, so it goes inside

parts.note: the setter's intent here is unclear; this outer part supplies the remaining letters
Con is short for Conservative, a political allegiance

explanation.surface: A newspaper man and his political views are welcomed by an official in Brussels.
explanation.walkthrough: The Telegraph is a Conservative newspaper, which gives the political leaning; how the outer letters come from European Union man is not clear from the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo Marconi pioneered wireless telegraphy, so he is the inventor associated with long-distance radio signalling.

clue.text: Domestic whose absenteeism is explained by nasty bender?

definitions.text: whose absenteeism is explained by nasty bender?
definitions.note: a cryptic description of the servant who gave her name to a knee ailment
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the worker whose name is attached to an inflamed knee, a bender being the joint that bends

explanation.walkthrough: A bender looks like a drinking spree, but here it is a knee; housemaid's knee is the old name for bursitis of the kneecap, caused by kneeling to scrub.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic is a household servant, and this particular servant does cleaning and tidying in a home.

clue.text: A sign of fleas for Hitler, perhaps?

definitions.note: the answer is the letter that begins the name, not the man

parts.note: taken as written
flea bites make the skin itch

explanation.surface: Scratching suggests a dictator has caught fleas.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the spelt-out name of the letter that opens Hitler's name, so Hitler is a loose example of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The spelt name of the eighth letter of the alphabet, which is the initial of the dictator's surname.

clue.text: Decided to do away with a desire

indicators.note: doing away with something removes it from the word

parts.note: to have agreed is to have decided together
the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: Someone resolved to get rid of a longing.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed is an excessive craving for wealth, food or possessions, so a strong selfish wanting.

clue.text: What does 23 across do in the autumn? Makes pastry

definitions.text: What does 23 across do in the autumn?
definitions.note: a question answered by a phrase, read as drops cone
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a conifer sheds a seed case when the season turns
second meaning: a small thick pancake cooked on a griddle

explanation.surface: The monkey puzzle tree sheds in autumn and somehow bakes a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as drops cone and it says what the tree at 23-across does in autumn. Pastry is loose: a drop scone is a Scottish griddle pancake.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop scone is a small baked item spooned onto a griddle, a teatime treat loosely counted among pastries.

clue.text: Distinctive feature of alien mutating with humans to get Tory leader

indicators.note: a leader is the front letter of a word
something mutating changes form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
men are humans in the general sense
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sci-fi tale of an alien crossbreeding with people to produce the Conservative leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineaments are the characteristic lines or contours of a face or body, so a defining trait.

clue.text: Being daffy, he fell for himself in the water

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the plant genus that includes the daffodil

definitions.text: he fell for himself in the water
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the youth of Greek myth who loved his own reflection in a pool

explanation.walkthrough: Daffy suggests silly; it is daffodil-like. In the myth the youth fell in love with his reflection; fell also hints at falling in.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissus is both the botanical name of the daffodil family and the mythical beauty who loved his own reflection.

clue.text: Promising person holding food correspondent to be a bit of a dummy

indicators.note: holding means having it inside

parts.note: a comer is someone likely to succeed, an up-and-comer
Matthew Fort was the Guardian's food writer

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming person with a food writer in tow is a bit of an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: Dummy here is a baby's pacifier, not a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A comforter is a baby's rubber teat for sucking, which British English also calls a dummy.

clue.text: Shed on sale in Oxfam shop?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to throw off or discard
second meaning: secondhand clothing someone has discarded

explanation.walkthrough: Oxfam is a British charity whose high-street shops sell donated secondhand goods. Shed looks like a garden building but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast off is to discard; as a noun the word means unwanted garments given away, typical charity shop stock.

clue.text: Sea creature taken for hair-covered goddess

indicators.note: something covered has another layer wrapped round it

parts.note: a mane is a long growth of hair
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A marine animal is mistaken for a hairy goddess, as sailors once mistook such animals for mermaids.
explanation.definitionFit: The manatee, or sea cow, is a large plant-eating aquatic mammal of warm coastal waters.

clue.text: Scottish pair, not great leaders, sound American

definitions.note: a noun phrase: a nasal sound typical of American speech

parts.note: twa is Scots for two

indicators.note: leaders are the opening letters of words

parts.note: the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Two Scots who are poor at leading speak with an American accent.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a nasal quality of speech, the kind associated with American accents.

clue.text: Some authors (at last I'm included) find the vertical angle

indicators.note: what is included is put inside
some of a word means only part of it is used

parts.note: the first part of the word
Z is the last letter, as in A to Z
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some writers, the setter among them at last, discover an angle.
explanation.walkthrough: At last looks like a phrase meaning finally; it is the letter that comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Azimuth is the angle around the horizon measured to the vertical circle through a body, used in astronomy and navigation.

clue.text: Other men with girl means there's trouble in the air

definitions.note: a clause describing what the answer, a noun, signifies

indicators.note: other means different, so the letters are made into something different

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl with other men suggests trouble brewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gremlins were imaginary imps blamed by RAF airmen for mechanical faults in aircraft.

clue.text: Does wrong to conceal bend in passage

indicators.note: concealing something means hiding it inside

parts.note: to sin is to do wrong
a U-bend, a bend in a pipe

explanation.surface: Someone misbehaves by hiding a turn in a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinus is an air-filled cavity or channel in the skull, so a passage in anatomy.

clue.text: Araucaria's not so hot, they say: show how sad you are!

indicators.note: what they say is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: chilly means cool, not so hot
to pine is to yearn sadly

explanation.surface: Araucaria, the famous setter, is a bit under the weather, so show sympathy.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria is the Latin genus of the monkey puzzle and the pseudonym of a celebrated Guardian setter; the possessive is read as Araucaria is.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chile pine is another name for the monkey puzzle tree, Araucaria araucana, native to Chile.

clue.text: Aristocrat losing some French game

indicators.note: losing something takes it out of the word

parts.note: a duchess is a noblewoman
du is French for some, as in du pain

explanation.surface: A noble loses a French game.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is the two-player board game of strategy, with kings, queens and pawns.

clue.text: Delete in under a second

indicators.note: the letters sit in the words that follow

parts.note: the run across the end of the first word, the second, and start of the third

explanation.surface: Wiping something in less than a second.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to rub out or wipe away, as with deleting text or data.

clue.text: Declare proclivities inverted as a result

definitions.note: the clue reads as a result

indicators.note: inverting the two-word phrase puts its second word first

parts.note: to come out is to declare one's sexuality

explanation.surface: A person comes out and turns things upside down as a consequence.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words of the phrase swap places rather than letters being read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome is the consequence or end effect of an action or event.

clue.text: Marine bird or beast pinned its ear back

indicators.note: pinning something holds it fast inside

parts.note: a seal is a marine animal

indicators.note: back means the word is read the other way

parts.note: lug is slang for ear

explanation.surface: A seabird or animal has had its ear flattened back.
explanation.definitionFit: A seagull is a gull, a common bird of coasts and the sea.

clue.text: Charges about two sovereigns for tentative suggestions

indicators.note: about means around, so one word surrounds the rest

parts.note: fees are charges for a service
L for a pound coin, the sovereign being a gold pound, plus ER, Elizabeth Regina, a reigning monarch

explanation.surface: Charges covering two gold coins as an opening offer.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is both a gold one-pound coin (L, from Latin libra) and a monarch (ER, for Queen Elizabeth).
explanation.definitionFit: Feelers are cautious approaches put out to test opinion, like an insect's antennae testing the way.

clue.text: Boy's female relation by marriage?

parts.note: step- relations are acquired by a parent's marriage
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: A boy wonders about a woman related to him through marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen is a male first name, so an example of what a boy might be called.
